source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every figure read from the page image; the same figures in the Banbridge Chronicle, 30 May 1908, p. 3

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1908: polled 27 May 1908 in twelve divisions; the other nine (ten seats) returned unopposed, Killeavy by the sitting member being deemed re-elected for want of a nomination. Majority 88. Thomas M'Crum withdrew (Armagh Guardian, 8 May 1908, p. 6). Described in the nominations as: Robert R. Murphy, J.P. (anti-direct labour); Robert G. M'Crum, D.L. (direct labour).
